_added_05-09-2026: ADNOCDIST and PHAR were added when this gate's BLEND pattern was widened to admit CENTRE as well as CENTRAL -- every alternative in it spelled the noun one way, so a document using the other read as clean. THEY ARE NOT THE SAME DEFECT AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT. ADNOCDIST is a real blend in BOTH the words and the arithmetic: its Table 1 prints 'WEIGHTED CENTRE - Frame A' with the weights beside it and its published 4.4113 reproduces to 8.9e-16 as 0.40 cash flow + 0.25 normalised + 0.20 relative + 0.15 BOOK, which this rule forbids twice over -- once as a blend and once because book value is a disclosed floor that is never weighted. It carries no lens_record at all, so the design gate cannot see it either. PHAR is the opposite shape: its committed weights are 1.0/0.0/0.0/0.0, the cash-flow lens carrying everything and the other three nothing, which IS one class primary being the central -- its record correctly declares a two-sided primary whose range contains both frames. What is wrong there is only the PROSE, still calling the answer a 'weighted centre' in vocabulary inherited from the architecture this rule retired. A reader is told the study publishes a blend when it publishes one lens read. Neither is repaired here: re-issuing a delivered study is an explicitly-requested step, not something done in passing.
